scenarios.name: full-commarea

commarea.CA-DATA: Plain text error message from a caller

scenarios.why: EIBCALEN 90, the longest the oracle judges: 'COMMAREA=' + 81 bytes; LENGTH 90 + 5 = 95 = WRITE-MSG, so TD CSMT and TS GENAERRS are written

scenarios.name: caller-error-record
scenarios.why: the shape a caller's WRITE-ERROR-MESSAGE sends (date, time, program, customer, policy, RESP) behind the 9-byte 'COMMAREA=' tag

scenarios.name: short-commarea
scenarios.why: EIBCALEN 40 (GenApp's IF EIBCALEN < 91 arm of the callers): LENGTH 40 + 5 = 45, only the first 45 bytes of WRITE-MSG are logged

scenarios.name: tiny-commarea
scenarios.why: EIBCALEN 10: the 9-byte tag and one byte of text

scenarios.name: blank-text
scenarios.why: EIBCALEN 90, CA-DATA blanks: the message is the tag and blanks

scenarios.name: full-text-bytes
scenarios.why: all 81 bytes of CA-DATA that fit under EIBCALEN 90

scenarios.name: terminal-queue-prefix
scenarios.why: INVOKINGPROG is blank (the oracle names no caller), so the RECEIVE arm runs: the line after the 5-byte transid is the message, and its leading 'Q=' makes the TS queue name GENA + the next 4 bytes and the message the 83 bytes after them (LENGTH - 7 + 5)

notes: GenApp's error logger (LGSTSQ), the program every GenApp program LINKs on a non-NORMAL RESP. LINKed with a COMMAREA (ASSIGN INVOKINGPROG is the caller's name, so the 'C' arm runs): COMMA-DATA (90 bytes) is the message, WRITEQ TD to CSMT and WRITEQ TS to GENAERRS (or GENA + the 4 bytes after a leading 'Q=') with LENGTH = EIBCALEN + 5 (- 7 for a 'Q=' prefix), the SYSID of the region in front. The case ships the LINKed arm only: the transaction arm (INVOKINGPROG blank: RECEIVE INTO, SEND TEXT) needs a started task, and a case is either LINKed or started. A COMMAREA longer than 90 bytes (the callers' 99-byte CA-ERROR-MSG, 101-byte ERROR-MSG) gives LENGTH > FROM on the WRITEQ TD, which the oracle refuses by name (oracle_assumptions.md X6): not here. The region ASSIGN SYSID is a deployment fact the corpus does not name.
